diagnostic_evidence.quote: bounded by twice the sum of the neglected singular values, multiplicities not counted,
let the distinct singular values of $\mathbf{\Sigma}_2$~be $\sigma_k$, with multiplicities $m_k $

issues.failure_explanation: Classical balanced truncation bounds the error by twice the neglected Hankel singular values counted with multiplicity, i.e. by 2 sum_k m_k sigma_k after grouping distinct values. The stated bound 2 sum_k sigma_k is smaller whenever some m_k>1, and the proof is explicitly not reproduced beyond a citation; the later teo5 argument does not justify deleting the factors m_k.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore multiplicity factors in the sum, equivalently state the bound as 2 sum_{i=r+1}^n sigma_i, or add a hypothesis that all neglected singular values are simple.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised sharpness of the SLS balanced-truncation error estimate is unreliable whenever a neglected singular value is multiple.
issues.title: Balanced-truncation error bound drops neglected-singular-value multiplicities
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and leaves the same type of error guarantee, but it withdraws the claimed improvement for non-simple neglected singular values.

issues.failure_explanation: For a general Hurwitz matrix A, sigma_min(I⊗A+A⊗I) is not determined by sigma_min(A); the equality used in prop1 and later in the rescaling estimate is false for nonnormal A. Thus the certified denominator 2 sigma_min(A) is not a valid lower bound for sigma_min(calL), and the O(n) certification story based only on sigma_min(A) is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace sigma_min(A) by a certified lower bound for sigma_min(calL) or an equivalent stability margin; the source gives no complete repair that keeps the same O(n) computability from sigma_min(A) alone.
issues.overall_effect: teo1's computable GLE error bound, the stopping criteria built from it, and the claimed sparse O(n) certification all become unreliable for nonnormal A.
issues.title: False singular-value identity for the Lyapunov operator
issues.why_classification: The main certified-solver result loses its stated computable guarantee in a regime not excluded by the hypotheses; a valid replacement requires a different operator stability quantity.

issues.failure_explanation: Even with gamma=1, teo1 still contains ||R_{k-1}||/(2 sigma_min(A)), and the current residual enters with weight 1/sigma_min(A); the two displayed requirements therefore do not imply ||X-tilde X_k||_2 <= tol unless the previous residual is also controlled or monotonicity is assumed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the same residual bound for R_{k-1}, or explicitly use the subsequent dynamically updated tol_Lyap rule; this is a local correction to the stopping rule.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised user-tolerance stopping guarantee can fail if only the current residual and Delta_{k,k-1} are enforced.
issues.title: Static stopping rule ignores the previous Lyapunov residual
issues.why_classification: A short additional residual condition or the already stated dynamic tolerance restores the guarantee without changing the theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: Dissipativity bounds w^T A_j^T w by the negative largest eigenvalue of (A_j+A_j^T)/2, not by -sigma_n(A_j)||w||^2. For nonnormal dissipative A_j the smallest singular value can be much larger than that margin, so mu >= kappa(A_j)||X-tilde X|| need not dominate the possibly positive term w^T tilde E A_j^T w.

failure_location.quote: where we used the fact that $\fw^{\T}\fA_j^{\T}\fw<0$ for all $\fw\in\R^{\stateDim}\setminus \{\zeroVec\}$ due to \eqref{eqn:ass:ndeAj}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use alpha_j = -lambda_max((A_j+A_j^T)/2) and require mu >= max_j sigma_1(A_j)/alpha_j ||X-tilde X||_2; this valid rule can be arbitrarily larger than the stated kappa-based rule as alpha_j becomes small.
issues.overall_effect: The constructed perturbation hat X = tilde X + mu I is not guaranteed to satisfy the reachability LMI under the stated mu rule; the later eqn:cond:LMI choice inherits this gap.
issues.title: teo4 uses sigma_n(A_j) where the dissipative margin is required
issues.why_classification: The sufficient perturbation can degrade from O(kappa tol) to an arbitrarily larger quantity while the dissipative margin tends to zero, so the stated stability-preserving perturbation guarantee is not comparable to a valid one.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For simplicity, let us assume $\tilde m=m(j)$ for all $j\in\switchingSet$

issues.failure_explanation: The jump map W_{q_k}^T V_{q_{k-1}} sends R^{r_{q_{k-1}}} to R^{r_{q_k}}. If r_j differ, the state dimension changes at a switching instant and the displayed ODE does not define one fixed-state-space switched system; a common reduced dimension is only reintroduced later for the error analysis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Enforce one common reduced dimension for all modes in the construction of eqn:new:red:system, for example by truncating every mode to the same r or embedding all modes in a common reduced space.
issues.overall_effect: The PBR reduced switched system is not well-defined as a single dynamical system unless a common reduced dimension is imposed before the jump matrices are used.
issues.title: Piecewise balancing reduction allows mode-dependent state dimension
issues.why_classification: The construction can be repaired by a contained common-dimension restriction, but the procedure as stated loses the fixed state-space needed for the subsequent stability and error statements.

issues.failure_explanation: With C_j of size outDim by stateDim, C_j C_j^T is outDim by outDim and cannot be added to the stateDim by stateDim matrix; the appendix itself uses the different, dimensionally correct matrix A_j^T Sigma_j + Sigma_j A_j + C_j^T C_j while still calling its largest eigenvalue lambda_1(fM_o(j)).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace fM_o(j) by bar A_j^T Sigma_j + Sigma_j bar A_j + bar C_j^T bar C_j; the appendix already uses this expression, so the repair is forced and local.
issues.overall_effect: The definition of fM_o, and hence the H_o term built from it in teo5 and reused in teo6, is not the observability operator unless the transposes are corrected.
issues.title: Observability matrix fM_o in teo5 has wrong transposes and dimensions
issues.why_classification: The intended matrix is explicitly used in the appendix, so correcting the displayed definition restores consistency without changing the claimed bound.

issues.failure_explanation: The definition reuses k as the bound of the sum defining s_k, so s_k does not depend on k and m_r=r is inserted as a multiplicity. The intended cumulative reduced dimensions would be s_k=r+sum_{i=r+1}^k m_i, and the first error term should sum tilde sigma_k, not tilde sigma_{s_k}; moreover H_{c,o,switch}(s_{k+1},s_k) must specify which truncated balanced system the teo5 quantities refer to.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: At minimum, define cumulative reduced dimensions s_k=r+sum_{i=r+1}^k m_i, replace tilde sigma_{s_k} by tilde sigma_k, and state precisely that the H/G factors are evaluated for the balanced system truncated from s_{k+1} to s_k; no such repaired statement is present.
issues.overall_effect: The final PBR error bound is not an evaluable formula as stated; the neglected-singular-value term and the H/G correction terms cannot be assigned unambiguously.
issues.title: teo6 cumulative indices s_k and sigma_{s_k} are not well-defined
issues.why_classification: The central advertised error estimate is formally ill-posed, and repairing it requires rewriting its indexing and the meaning of the H/G arguments rather than a single forced typo fix.

issues.failure_explanation: When the H or G argument is negative, the Heaviside factor selects that case but the displayed power is still the square root of the negative argument. The intended positive-part terms are (H)_{+}^{1/2} and -(-G)_{+}^{1/2}; as written the real-valued correction is undefined exactly in the cases the Heaviside factors are meant to handle.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use positive-part notation, (H)_{+}^{1/2} and -(-G)_{+}^{1/2}, in eqn:err:est:3 and in eqn:chi/eqn:iota.
issues.overall_effect: The signed correction terms in teo6, and the numerical definitions chi and iota copied from them, are not well-defined for negative H or G values.
issues.title: Heaviside terms in teo6 take square roots of possibly negative arguments
issues.why_classification: The correction is a forced local positive-part notation change and does not alter the intended bound.

issues.failure_explanation: A_1 has a nonzero subdiagonal, and A_2 has subdiagonal magnitude 4/5 but superdiagonal magnitude 1/5, so A_j A_j^T != A_j^T A_j. The normality justification is false; the needed dissipativity of teo4 still holds for these matrices by a direct eigenvalue check, so the example is repairable by changing the reason.

failure_location.quote: Moreover, both $\fA_1$ and $\fA_2$ are normal matrices, so the hypothesis of \Cref{teo4} holds.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the normality claim by a direct check that A_1+A_1^T and A_2+A_2^T are negative definite.
issues.overall_effect: The stated verification of the teo4 hypothesis is based on a false matrix property, although the hypothesis itself remains true for this example.
issues.title: Synthetic example falsely claims A_1 and A_2 are normal
issues.why_classification: The conclusion for the example survives after a local justification change, so there is no loss of the demonstrated result.

issues.failure_explanation: For outDim=2 and stateDim=1000, C^T C^T is not an n by n matrix and is not the observability operator; the correct term is C^T C. The displayed operator used for the tightening table is therefore dimensionally invalid as written.
issues.overall_effect: The largest-eigenvalue values reported in tab:2 are tied to an incorrectly transcribed operator, although the intended observability residual is clear.
issues.title: Observability residual operator in eqn:def:N has an incompatible transpose
issues.why_classification: The forced transpose correction restores a dimensionally valid and intended operator with no change to the numerical conclusion.
